title: surveyframe .sframe file
description: Schema for the .sframe instrument format written by write_sframe() and read by read_sframe(). Documented so a reviewer or a second tool can read and validate a .sframe file without installing the R package -- the file is plain UTF-8 JSON, not an R-specific or binary format. Every field here corresponds to a key produced by sframe_serialization_payload() in R/read_write_sframe.R and R/amendments.R.

sframe_format.description: The .sframe format version (SFRAME_FORMAT_VERSION in R/read_write_sframe.R), written as the first key of every file. Distinct from `version` below, which is the instrument's own version, and from the surveyframe package version. Absent in files written before 2026-08-22, which remain valid and still verify, since the hash is computed over whatever the file contains. Not listed in `required` for that reason. Conformance profiles key on this value.

hash.description: File-level integrity hash. Confirms the file on disk is byte-identical to what write_sframe() produced. Not a proof of methodological validity -- see the `amendments` field below for the disclosed-revision mechanism, and the package's analysis-plan binding (run_analysis_plan()) for the package's separate anti-HARKing safeguard.

value.description: SHA-256 digest (64 lowercase hex characters) computed over the canonical JSON serialisation of every other top-level field, with this field itself set to an empty string during hashing.

version.description: The instrument's own semantic version string (sf_instrument()'s `version` argument), not the surveyframe package version.

meta.description: Instrument metadata: title, description, authors, languages, and validation status.

analysis_plan.description: Pre-declared analysis-plan blocks, bound to the instrument at design time and executed in one pass by run_analysis_plan(). This binding, not the hash, is the package's defence against HARKing and p-hacking; the hash only proves file identity.

designs.description: Optional conjoint designs. Present only when the instrument declares at least one, so instruments that don't use this feature hash identically to files written before it existed.

amendments.description: Optional disclosed-revision log, appended to by amend_sframe(). Present only when the instrument has at least one recorded amendment, for the same backward-compatibility reason as `designs`. Each entry documents one legitimate, disclosed change -- it is not itself a proof of the change's scientific merit, only a structured record of what changed, why, and whether a second reviewer signed off.

reason_text.description: Free-text explanation. Always required and non-empty.

tier.description: "pipeline": routine data/collection hygiene (data_correction, bot_removal), low friction. "design": a change to the analysis plan or a model, which the design-time plan binding exists to guard against -- requires deviation_report.

deviation_report.description: Required (non-null, non-empty) when tier is "design": what changed in the research question, method, or model, and why. Not required for "pipeline" amendments.

signoff.description: A second reviewer's name/identifier, or the literal string "none" -- never blank, so an unreviewed design change is visible to an auditor rather than indistinguishable from a signed-off one.

previous_hash.description: SHA-256 content hash (64 hex chars) of the instrument's substantive fields (items/choices/scales/branching/checks/analysis_plan/models/designs, excluding `hash` and `amendments` themselves) immediately before this amendment. Distinct from the file-level `hash` field above -- see amend_sframe()'s documentation.

new_hash.description: The same content hash, computed immediately after this amendment.

changed_fields.description: Which top-level payload keys differed between previous_hash and new_hash's states, e.g. ["items"] or ["items", "analysis_plan"]. Not a full content diff -- narrows where to look, same design intent as the file-level hash mismatch message.
